faqs.q: How much should I salary sacrifice into super?
faqs.a: The amount you salary sacrifice depends on your tax bracket, financial goals, and the concessional contributions cap set by the Australian Taxation Office. A common strategy is to sacrifice enough to reduce your taxable income to a lower bracket, but this is not one-size-fits-all. For example, if you earn $100,000 and sacrifice $10,000, you save $3,000 in tax plus Medicare levy, while the super fund pays 15% contributions tax. Always consult a qualified financial adviser before deciding.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or agreement, set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for full-time adults. Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries or occupations, set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Most employees are covered by an award, so their minimum pay is likely above the National Minimum Wage.

Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, compensating for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour for casuals. When using the timesheet on this site, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% automatically. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you’re paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, the first step is to convert your hourly rate into an annual figure. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week (the standard under the Fair Work Act). That gives you 1,976 hours per year. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a part-time worker on 20 hours a week would use 20 × 52 = 1,040 hours.

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate your fortnightly pay (weekly pay × 2) and your take-home pay after tax and super.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The [National Minimum Wage](/topics/minimum-wage) from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a full-time adult employee, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets a higher minimum. Award rates vary by industry and occupation – for instance, a retail employee may have a different minimum than a hospitality worker. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award. If you’re not covered by an award, the National Minimum Wage applies.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that’s $33.05 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading – tick the checkbox instead.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. For 2026–27, the super guarantee applies up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your annual earnings exceed that, super is only paid on the first $270,830.

## Salary Sacrifice Into Super

Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you agree to forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for additional super contributions from your employer. This reduces your taxable income, so you pay less income tax and Medicare levy. The super fund pays a 15% contributions tax on the sacrificed amount (up to the concessional cap).

You might be wondering, **how much should I salary sacrifice into super?** The answer depends on your tax bracket and long-term goals. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed).

If you’re in the 30% bracket, each dollar sacrificed saves you 30¢ in tax plus 2¢ Medicare, but incurs 15¢ contributions tax – a net saving of 17¢. The higher your bracket, the greater the saving. However, you must stay within the annual concessional contributions cap (set by the ATO) to avoid extra tax. A common approach is to sacrifice enough to bring your taxable income down to the top of a lower bracket, but this is not right for everyone. Consult a financial adviser for personal advice.

### Estimating Your Take-Home Pay

Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator can help you see the effect of salary sacrifice. Remember that the annual pay shown here is an estimate: it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Fortnightly Pay Example

If your hourly rate is $30 and you work 38 hours a week, your weekly gross is $1,140. Fortnightly that’s $2,280. After tax and Medicare (assuming no other deductions), your take-home might be around $1,960, depending on your tax bracket. Super of 12% ($273.60 per week) is paid on top by your employer.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay. From there you can estimate tax and super. It’s a handy tool whether you’re comparing a salary offer or planning your budget.

For more detailed pay guides and award rates, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page. You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for tax brackets and super caps.

### Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time)
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour; most awards pay more
- Casual loading is 25% on top; do not include it in your base rate
- Super is 12% paid on top by your employer, up to $270,830
- Salary sacrifice reduces taxable income but has caps; consider your tax bracket
- Use the timesheet to estimate your pay, but remember it’s an estimate
